name: Brotato Cartoon
summary: Candy-bright HD vector cartoon: thick deep-plum outlines, one cel-shade crescent, one white gloss and bouncy squash & stretch.
description: A clean, high-resolution vector cartoon in the spirit of Brotato: every object is a chunky rounded silhouette with one thick deep-plum outline, a flat fill, exactly one darker cel-shade crescent and one white glossy highlight. Characters are big-headed, round and expressive (angry brows, googly eyes, carved grins) and bounce constantly with squash and stretch. The ground is a flat play-mat of soft-edged grass, lilac and sand regions sprinkled with tiny vector tufts and flowers, so the outlined actors pop clearly even in huge hordes.

difficulty.why: Shapes with an outline and flat colour are the most natural thing to generate in code: new enemies are quick to build and read well, and there is plenty of performance headroom.

technique.resolution: Native display resolution. Sprites are baked once at K = clamp(round(screenPx/360 * 1.25), 3, 6) canvas px per world unit (4 frames, normal + white-flash copy, both facings); ground chunks are rasterised at up to 3 px per world unit (groundResMax 3, chunkSize 256).
technique.summary: Each sprite is a list of parts painted twice into an offscreen canvas: an outline pass strokes+fills every part in plum (#3a2240) at 2x the outline weight, producing one merged silhouette outline, then a fill pass paints each part with base colour, a cel crescent (the shape clipped against itself shifted up-left) and a white gloss ellipse.
technique.linework: One outline colour only: deep plum #3a2240. Outer silhouette 1.15 world units (stroke width 2.3, half hidden under the fill), inner separation lines 0.55 units (stroke 1.1 inside the clip), small items 0.6–0.9 units. Round caps and joins everywhere; no black, no coloured outlines.
technique.shading: Flat fill plus exactly ONE cel step: the whole part is filled with its shade colour, then the lit colour is clipped to the same shape shifted by (-1..-2.8, -0.9..-2.6) units, leaving a crisp dark crescent on the lower-right. No gradients on bodies.
technique.lighting: Implied light from the top-left. One white gloss ellipse (alpha 0.92) near the top-left of each big shape plus a tiny white dot next to it. Warm additive glow (lighter blend) only for lanterns/candle light; carved faces glow #ffd43f with a #fff3b0 hot core.
technique.texture: None on actors. The ground has sparse vector decals (3-blade tufts, 5-petal flowers, pebbles, fallen leaves) and a ±3.5% low-frequency brightness tint.

palette.name: Plum Outline
palette.role: The only outline/ink colour: silhouettes, pupils, brows, mouths, HUD borders and text outlines

palette.name: Candle Glow
palette.role: Carved eyes/mouth, stars, crit numbers; hot core #fff3b0, carve rim #8a3214

palette.name: Brute Purple
palette.role: Large brute top; shade #58297a, bottom ochre #efc96f

paletteRules: Every colour comes as a pair: fill + one darker, slightly more saturated shade (about 15–25% darker, hue shifted warm or toward purple). Never a third tone on a body.
The outline is always #3a2240 – never pure black, never per-object outline colours.
Ground colours are desaturated and mid-light (meadow, lilac, sand) so the saturated actors (orange, purple, teal, white) dominate.
Highlights are pure white at 0.92 alpha; shadows on the ground are plum at 20% alpha, never grey or black.
Enemies use cool purples/whites, the hero warm orange + teal: the player always contrasts with the horde.
Glow colour #ffd43f is reserved for light sources, rewards and crits.

typography.role: Damage numbers, HUD numbers, clock, titles, card names
Body text, labels, card descriptions, hints
typography.css: font: 600 12px/1.2 'Fredoka', 'Baloo 2', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 1.6px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8a6280;

background.summary: A flat-colour play-mat: large calm regions (dark grass, lilac meadow, clay field, sand clearings and even-width winding sand paths) generated from low-frequency noise, rasterised with an analytic signed distance (value / gradient) so every region has a crisp anti-aliased edge and a slightly darker 1.7–2.5 unit inner rim band; tiny flat vector decals sit on top.
layers: Noise regions in order: dark grass #79ae5a (rim #6a9e50, 1.7u), lilac #c8b6da (rim #b4a0cc, 2.0u), clay #daa070 (rim #c78a60, 2.3u), sand clearings + paths #ebd3a0 (rim #d8ba85, 2.5u)
±3.5% brightness tint from very low-frequency noise (period ~1500 units)
Decals on a 12-unit jittered grid: 3-blade grass tufts (0.8 u strokes), 5-petal flowers (white/yellow/pink, orange centre), dot clusters, pebbles on sand, fallen leaves on clay
Batched plum ground shadows under all actors and props (one union path, one fill)
Spawn holes: dirt ring #b07a4c with plum outline and dark hole #43283f before enemies pop out
World overlay: butterflies drifting at z 16 with their own small shadows

characters.summary: Chunky, big-headed toy figures built from ellipses, capsules (limbs), Catmull-Rom blobs and rounded polygons. The hero (~25 u wide, ~37 u tall incl. stem at 1.1 scale) is a giant pumpkin head (rx 11.2, ry 9.1) on a tiny teal body with stubby capsule limbs, a waving scarf and a carved, glowing jack-o'-lantern face offset toward the facing side. 4 baked hop frames; squash & stretch, tilt and lift are applied at draw time.
rules: Head is ~60% of the height; bodies and limbs are tiny and stubby (limb radius 1.15–1.45 u).
All parts of a figure merge into ONE plum silhouette outline (outline pass first), inner overlaps get 0.55 u separation lines only where needed.
Every big shape gets its cel crescent toward the lower-right and its gloss ellipse at the upper-left.
Faces are drawn into the fill pass: googly white eyes with plum pupils and a white catchlight, thick angry brows (1.35 u), simple arc mouths; or carved shapes with dark rim + glowing offset inside.
Faces sit off-centre toward the facing direction; sprites are mirrored with scale(-1,1) for the other facing.
Each enemy class has a unique silhouette: round turnip waddler, tall ghost with wavy hem, 2.5x-size brute with bandages and teeth.
Pre-bake a white flash copy of every frame (fill = #ffffff, shade = #efe6f6) for hits.

effects.name: Projectile
effects.how: A cream seed (#fff1c8, shade #e6c68a, outline 0.85 u) spinning by squashing its height 0.55–1.0, trailed by a white speed streak: three round-cap lines (1.0 u and 0.75 u) with a linear gradient from 0.95 alpha to 0 over 14 units.

effects.name: Hit star
effects.how: An 8-point white star (outer 5.6, inner 2.6, rounded corners 0.4, shade #fff3b5) popping 0.5→1.2→0.3 scale over 0.14 s, plus a 4-point yellow-white spark flying off with gravity.

effects.name: Hit flash
effects.how: Blit the baked white-flash copy over the normal sprite at alpha min(0.85, flash*1.3) and squash the sprite (x*1+0.22f, y*1-0.18f).

effects.name: Death pop
effects.how: The enemy inflates in white to 1.28x over 0.22 s, wobbles and shrinks to nothing by 0.5 s; 6–9 outlined cloud puffs burst radially (outBack grow, quadratic shrink, rising 7 u), 2–6 yellow 5-point stars arc out with gravity and 4–10 outlined colour chunks of the enemy's colours bounce away.

effects.name: Shockwave ring
effects.how: A flat ellipse (ry = 0.45 rx) growing to 30 u with outQuad, stroked twice: plum at width w+1.4 under white/yellow at width w, w shrinking from 2.4 to 0.

effects.name: Dash smear
effects.how: Three white-flash after-images at alpha 0.42/i spaced 7 u behind the hero, hero stretched x*1.2 y*0.88, plus 4 cream dust puffs.

effects.name: Level-up
effects.how: Yellow ring, 10 stars in a circle and 18 confetti rectangles (6 colours, outlined 0.45 u) that flip by scaling their y by cos(t*9).

effects.name: Damage numbers
effects.how: Lilita One 9 u (crit 12.5 u), baked per value: plum stroke 0.3*fs, plum drop copy offset 0.09*fs down, then white fill or a #fff27a→#ffc93a→#ff8a2a gradient for crits; pop 0.3→1.35→1.0 scale, random tilt ±0.15 rad.

ui.summary: Chunky toy-like HUD: cream (#fff4de) pill panels and dark plum (#563a5e) bar troughs with a 4 px plum border, large radius and a solid 4–5 px plum drop 'lip' (box-shadow 0 5px 0) instead of blurred shadows. Bars have a 3-stop vertical gradient fill with a white 55–62% gloss strip inside. Numbers are Lilita One with a 16-direction plum text-shadow outline; labels are Fredoka 600 in muted mauve #8a6280. Level-up cards have a coloured header band (orange, mint, violet) and pop in with overshoot easing.

motion: Hero hops instead of walking: hop phase = anim*0.42, lift = sin(f*PI)*3.4 u; contact squash sx 1.12 / sy 0.87, airborne stretch sy 1.07; tilt 0.07 rad toward movement; frame 2 in the air, frames 1/3 alternate on contact; a dust puff on every landing.
Small enemies waddle: 4 frames at anim*0.85, rock ±0.1 rad, bob 1.3 u, squash 5–6% at contact.
Ghosts float 4.5 u up with a ±1.6 u bob (t*2.6), cycle 4 hem frames at 7 fps, wobble 4%, lean into velocity up to 0.16 rad.
Brutes stomp: anim*0.32, lift 2 u, contact squash 8% with a cubic contact curve, rock 0.035 rad.
Spawns: enemies pop out of a dirt hole with outElastic vertical stretch; ghosts fade in with outBack scale.
Pickups bob 1.1 u at t*5 with 4–5% squash; props sway by skewing around their base (trees 0.025, bushes 0.035 at t*1.3).
Every pop uses overshoot easing (outBack / outElastic / cubic-bezier(.3,1.7,.5,1)).
do: Use ONE outline colour (#3a2240) and draw the outline as a separate pass so all parts merge into one silhouette.
Give every shape exactly one cel crescent (shape clipped against itself, offset up-left) and one white gloss ellipse at the top-left.
Keep shapes fat and rounded: ellipses, capsules, blobs, rounded polygons with corner radius ≥ 0.4 u.
Bake sprites once at K px per unit and only transform them at draw time (squash, stretch, tilt, flip).
Animate everything with squash & stretch and overshoot easing – nothing should move rigidly.
Keep the ground flat and pastel with crisp region edges, so outlined actors pop.
Batch all ground shadows into one path and one translucent plum fill so overlapping shadows do not darken.
Pre-bake white flash copies for hit feedback.
dont: Don't use black or per-object outline colours, and don't vary outline thickness randomly.
Don't add gradients, textures or noise to character bodies – only the flat fill + one crescent + gloss.
Don't draw thin, spiky or realistic anatomy; no hard 90° corners.
Don't outline the ground regions or decals – the ground is outline-free so it stays behind the actors.
Don't use blurred drop shadows or grey shadows; use flat plum ellipses at 20% alpha and solid offset lips in the UI.
Don't re-path every part every frame for hundreds of enemies – that kills performance; blit baked sprites.
Don't let the ground become as saturated as the actors (no pure greens or bright purples underfoot).
performance: All characters, props, pickups and particles are baked once in init() (4 frames x normal + flash + mirrored copies; ~60 canvases total) – per frame it is only drawImage with transforms, so 300+ enemies run well. Ground chunks (256 u) are computed as generators: noise fields on a coarse 4-unit grid, per-pixel signed-distance work only in cells that touch a region edge (others are flat-filled); decals are baked into the chunk. Damage-number sprites are cached per value (cleared at 500). Shadows are one batched path per frame. Main cost: chunk generation when moving fast; cap groundResMax at 3.
